meta.scope: Thailand Batch 3 — Agriculture (rice/rubber), Eastern Economic Corridor, and fiscal/public debt densification.

candidates.title: Agriculture production statistics
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Cooperatives / NSO related
candidates.description: Official volume and value statistics for major crops and livestock. Rice and rubber are the two highest-centrality agricultural commodities; other significant products include sugarcane, cassava, palm oil and fruits.

candidates.title: Rice production and export statistics
candidates.description: Focused statistics on rice production, area and exports. Thailand is a major global rice exporter; the crop remains central to rural livelihoods and food-security framing.
candidates.notes: Foundational food and export crop node.

candidates.title: Natural rubber production and export statistics
candidates.description: Statistics on natural rubber planting area, production (dry rubber content) and exports. Thailand is among the world’s largest rubber producers and exporters; the southern region dominates production.

candidates.title: Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) policy and investment framing
candidates.publisher: Eastern Economic Corridor Office / Government of Thailand
candidates.description: Flagship regional development and investment corridor covering the eastern seaboard provinces. Targets high-value industries, infrastructure and skills upgrading; continuously cited in industrial, FDI and spatial-strategy analysis.

candidates.title: Public debt statistics
candidates.publisher: Public Debt Management Office / Ministry of Finance
candidates.description: Official statistics on public debt stock, composition (government, SOE, guarantees) and debt-to-GDP ratio. Recent readings place public debt in the mid-60s percent of GDP range.

candidates.title: Thailand agriculture–EEC–fiscal densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from agricultural, EEC and fiscal sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding agriculture and rice/rubber statistics, Eastern Economic Corridor framing, and public debt statistics into a coherent primary-sector, spatial-industrial and fiscal layer.
